Use the LuceneCountOperator also for ungrouped count(field) queries

pr_comments: I think this optimization doesn't account for cases where a field has multiple values in a document.

> I think this optimization doesn't account for cases where a field has multiple values in a document.

You are correct @dnhatn.

`from employees | where emp_no == 10010 | stats c = count(job_positions) by job_positions`

```
       c       |  job_positions  
---------------+-----------------
4              |Architect        
4              |Purchase Manager 
4              |Reporting Analyst
4              |Tech Lead        
```

> Unrelated to this specific PR.... I want to point out a behavior that for me seems slightly confusing.

Related and potentially unexpected:

`from hosts | keep ip0 | stats c=count(ip0) by ip0 | sort c | limit 1` returns:
```
       c       |      ip0      
---------------+---------------
0              |null           
```
, but dropping argument from `count()`: `from hosts | keep ip0 | stats c=count() by ip0 | sort c | limit 1` returns:
```
       c       |      ip0      
---------------+---------------
1              |null           

```
which makes sense, the latter counting the groups and former the values within the group (and `null` being no value), but we could document this -- currently the count docs don't mention the latter functionality.

Scratch that, I forgot that our csv tests are also being run against full server instances. So the tests are all good, of course :)

issue_context.title: ESQL: search-level count for a given field
issue_context.body:
### Description

Extension of #99602, to support counting a field when a filter/query already exists. This means creating an operator that extends the query and adds an exists clause for said field (to avoid counting nulls).

review_comments: nit: the lambda passed to `computeIfAbsent` is beginning to become a bit hard to read (I have trouble figuring out what exactly the lambda is trying to achieve). Consider factoring this into a well-named helper method or adding a comment.
int is a better default that prevents subtle conversion errors when trying to convert the null Integer to `int`.
can you please explain a little more about the situation causing errors? is there any doc regarding the same?

nit: the variable name used in the `rules` method is clearer (needed to look this up to understand what's going on), consider renaming:
```suggestion
    private final boolean optimizeForEsSource;
```
Is commenting this out intentional or a leftover?
It's commented out on purpose, just the like System.out so it doesn't load overload the server.
The eval trips the optimization - I'll work on a separate PR that fixes that in the Logical planner.
For the time being, could we comment that this is not the optimal plan? (e.g. by leaving a `TODO`)
I've added a TODO.

thought (out of scope of this PR): there's a subtle semantics issue here; normally we don't count `null`s, but since we treat every foldable expression the same, this means that `count(null)` returns the same as `count(*)`, while it would be more consistent to return `0`.
Raised https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/100170
The test setup is duplicated from PhysicalPlanOptimizerTests
Haha, I also had to introduce this for [another PR](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/99961/files). This setup looks more complete, though.
Thanks - let's serialize the two PRs and get this one through first (I'm biased I know).

I think we should also assert that the query `e < 10050` is correctly pushed into the `EsStatsQueryExec`.

Applies also below.

The filter push down is orthogonal to this test which checks that the stat has been detected, regardless of the filter of the underlying source.
Furthermore we have tests (in the PhysicalOptimizerTests) that covered this - I moved them here.

Nit:
```suggestion
              from test
              | eval s = salary | rename s as sr
              | eval hidden_s = sr
              | rename emp_no as e
              | where e < 10050
              | stats c = count(hidden_s)
```
or some other line breaking approach.
leftover; here and below.
is this check necessary (given the following one)? Or is it meant as an optimisation, to avoid reducing the stats if not necessary?

Yes since the rule might pick up two different fields however at runtime we don't know how to combine the operators.
For example `count(salary), count(emp_no) by gender` - this results into one EsStatsQuery with two Stat however because these are two different queries, two different sources are required and we currently allow only one.

Below we depend on having exactly one stat, so we should check this to avoid harder to find out of bounds exceptions.
```suggestion
        if ((statsQuery.stats().size() == 1) == false) {
```
